parsed.headline: Trump administration lifts some tariffs on Canadian imports

pages.text: The White House announced on Friday that it is lifting certain tariffs on Canadian imports to better serve the public interest. The decision includes exemptions for nine agricultural products, such as blueberries, potatoes, apples, and seaweed, as well as processing equipment including plywood sheets, packing boxes, paper products, certain machinery, and refrigeration equipment. Senator Susan Collins, a Republican from Maine, stated she had lobbied administration officials for relief, noting that many Maine farmers rely on specialized Canadian equipment and materials that are unavailable from American suppliers or too expensive to replace. Collins is currently in a tight re-election campaign against Democrat Troy Jackson, a former logger and Maine state senator, in a race considered a toss-up that could impact Democratic efforts to flip control of Congress during the November 3 midterms. While some tariffs are being removed, the White House specified it will levy new Section 338 tariffs on certain products, including carpets, specific valves, and waste products, to address what it described as Canada's discriminatory treatment of U.S. commerce. These new measures are scheduled to take effect on October 30.

parsed.headline: President Mahama joins Ethiopian Prime Minister to commission Megech Irrigation Project

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama arrived in Gondar, Ethiopia, on Friday, October 23, 2026, to join Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali in commissioning the Megech Irrigation Development Project. The visit to Ethiopia was made at the invitation of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali and precedes the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa scheduled to be held in Bahir Dar. Following his arrival at Gondar Airport, President Mahama and the Prime Minister officially commissioned the dam and reservoir infrastructure, which is designed to transform regional agriculture and water supply. The project, which began 18 years ago, reportedly stalled for several years until Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali revived and completed it three years ago. Spanning 870 hectares with a storage capacity of 185 million cubic metres, the Megech Dam is expected to support the irrigation of 17,000 hectares of agricultural land and provide clean, potable water to the city of Gondar and surrounding satellite towns. President Mahama commended the Ethiopian government and people for their resilience in delivering the project. President Mahama is expected to travel to Bahir Dar on October 24, 2026, to chair the 12th Tana High-Level Forum, an event intended to convene African leaders, policymakers, and security experts to discuss peace, governance, and security challenges across the continent.

parsed.headline: Two Syrian security members killed during anti-ISIS operation in Damascus countryside

pages.text: Two members of Syria’s Internal Security Forces were killed and five others were injured during a security operation targeting an Islamic State (ISIS) cell in Rankous, located in the western Damascus countryside, according to a statement from the security forces. The operation, which took place on a Thursday, was reportedly carried out in cooperation with General Intelligence. This information was reported by the North Press Agency.

parsed.headline: Inaugural Climate x Culture Summit held in Accra, Ghana

pages.text: The inaugural Climate x Culture Summit 2026 took place on October 22, 2026, at the Google AI Community Centre in Accra, Ghana. Organized by CultureJoint in partnership with the Office of the Minister of State in charge of Climate Change and Sustainability at the Office of the President, the event brought together climate practitioners, creative industry leaders, researchers, media professionals, financial sector representatives, and technology innovators. Under the theme “Designing Sustainable Creative Experiences for Africa,” the summit explored how music, the arts, cultural heritage, storytelling, and technology can influence public attitudes and encourage sustainable practices in Africa. 1

The summit opened with remarks from Kenneth Awotwe Darko, founder of CultureJoint and Climate x Culture Summit Lead, followed by a keynote address from Ruth Dzokoto, representing the Ministry of Climate Change and Sustainability. Messages of solidarity were delivered by media executive Ruddy Kwakye and Priscilla Adomaah Nsonwaah of the Centre for CSR, West Africa. A musical performance by Eli Six30, also known as The Village Boy, followed the opening ceremony. 2

A panel titled “The Big Picture: Climate × Culture — Why Creativity Matters in the Climate Decade” was moderated by Derick Ashilevi. The panel included Dr. Enoch Bessah, Lead for Climate Change and Ecosystem Services Monitoring at the DIPPER Lab at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST); Valerie Kplorm Nutakor, Programme Coordinator at the Climate and Development Knowledge Network (CDKN); musician and climate activist Okyeame Kwame; and Betty Osei Bonsu Adjei, Director of Operations and Programmes at the Green Africa Youth Organization (GAYO). 3

parsed.headline: Bangladesh Bank website remains offline following global cybersecurity alert

pages.text: The website of Bangladesh Bank (BB) remained offline on October 23, 2026, one day after the central bank took the site down as a precaution following a global cybersecurity alert. According to The Daily Star Bangladesh, the site has been inaccessible since noon on October 23, 2026, and was still down at the time of the report at 1:00 p.m. Visitors currently see a notice stating the service is undergoing scheduled maintenance and will be back online shortly. The central bank originally took the site down on October 22, 2026, after receiving the alert. This move follows emergency steps taken worldwide after critical flaws were disclosed in PHP, a widely used programming language. Cybersecurity firms Calif and Wiz uncovered these flaws using artificial intelligence tools; while patches were released, details became public before fixes could be fully applied. Arief Hossain Khan, executive director and spokesperson for the central bank, stated that the bank is still observing the situation to ensure full security, which is why the website has not been restored. Khan added that the IT department is working on the issue but did not provide a timeline for restoration. He noted that the connection between the central bank and commercial banks is running smoothly.

parsed.headline: President visits Dr. Abdul Moyeen Khan at Evercare Hospital in Bangladesh

pages.text: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir visited Dr. Abdul Moyeen Khan, the Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives, at Evercare Hospital in the capital on Friday morning. According to Bangabhaban, the President enquired about the minister’s health and treatment and wished him a speedy recovery during the visit. Hospital physicians, including cardiologist Prof Dr Shahabuddin Talukder, briefed the President on the minister's current medical condition. The minister’s wife, Advocate Roksana Khandaker, was present at the time of the visit. Dr. Moyeen Khan was admitted to the hospital on Wednesday night with respiratory distress and heart-related complications and remains under close medical observation.

parsed.headline: Retired general discusses potential U.S. and Israeli bombing campaign against Iran

pages.text: In an interview with NPR, retired Army four-star General Joseph Votel discussed U.S. and Israeli objectives regarding a potential post-election bombing campaign in Iran. Votel, who chaired Central Command from 2016 through 2019 overseeing military operations across the Middle East and currently chairs the Combating Terrorism Center at West Point, addressed the potential impact of new strikes. Votel stated that while a new strike could degrade Iran, it is unlikely to settle the war, noting that many of the targets have been hit previously.

parsed.headline: Conservation efforts and scientific studies focus on snow leopard coexistence in Nepal

pages.text: A 2025 government survey found approximately 397 snow leopards living in Nepal. According to Mongabay reporting, snow leopards in Asia’s mountain ranges face threats from climate change, declining wild prey, and retaliatory killings by local herders. A study published earlier this year in Nepal’s Lapchi Valley revealed that snow leopards, common leopards, and Himalayan wolves coexist in the region, largely by targeting different prey species. For example, wild blue sheep make up nearly half of the snow leopard’s prey. Narayan Prasad Koju, the study's lead researcher, told Mongabay that maintaining wild ungulate populations is critical to preventing predators from shifting toward livestock, which can trigger retaliatory killings and destabilize the system.

Rodney Jackson, the founder and board president of the U.S.-based Snow Leopard Conservancy, told Mongabay that conservationists should prioritize the immediate needs of herding families over population monitoring. Jackson noted that human-wildlife conflict undermines trust among local communities who bear the costs of living alongside the cats. He called for community support measures, including improved notification systems for when snow leopards are near livestock, camera-trap-triggered deterrents, and fair financial relief for livestock losses.
